THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 05.06.2025,
THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NO. 4987 OF 2025  2  2025:KER:395  BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.
 ......................................................
 B.A. No.4987 of 2025  ...................................................
 Dated this the 5th day of June, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.267/2025 of Munambom Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, and 468 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The prosecution case is that, accused had with the ulterior intention of making unlawful gain for themselves and causing unlawful loss to the de facto complainant, created forged certificates of the Land Tribunal, Ernakulam; in respect of a land which was not in the ownership of the accused.

Thereafter the accused is alleged to have entered into an agreement for the sale of the land with the de facto complainant, and received an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- as advance, and later refused to execute the sale deed or return the amount, and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners have been falsely arrayed as an accused and they have no involvement BAIL APPL. NO. 4987 OF 2025 2025:KER:39577 in the alleged crime.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are serious in nature and custodial interrogation is essential.

sentences.text: 7. On a perusal of the documents produced, as well as the FIR, it is noticed that, petitioners are alleged to have forged purchase certificates and collected advances from the de facto complainant for the sale of the property.

8. Though the allegations are serious, this Court notices that, as per Annexure-II order, the Land Tribunal, Ernakulam directed a purchase certificate to be issued to the petitioners, pursuant to which, Annexure-III purchase certificate is purported to have been issued.
Though it requires to be verified whether it relates to the same property, I am of the view that custodial interrogation is not necessary.

9. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.

10. On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this BAIL APPL. NO. 4987 OF 2025 2025:KER:39577 Court is of the view that though the allegations are serious in nature, custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not required.
Further, having regard to the nature of offence and the severity of punishment,this Court is of the view that petitioners are entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.

11. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 17.06.2025 and shall subject themselves to interrogation.
(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioners, then, they shall be released on bail on each of them executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only)
with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioners shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall they tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioners shall not commit any similar offences while they are on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications,
if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
